title: FactoryTrigger
description: Something that starts a Software Factory workflow: a GitHub webhook event, a finding, an issue label, a kanban card move, a firewall sighting, or a person pressing Run. A trigger is a trigger node in the workflow's graph whose id is metadata.name (at most 40 characters), so applying one saves and publishes a new version of the workflow, the same as adding the trigger in the workflow builder; the workflow must be published and must not hold an unpublished draft. A trigger node the workflow already has under that id is adopted. A schedule is a FactorySchedule. Conditions are typed fields: the console takes no expression for a trigger. A trigger is on while its workflow is on. Removing the document removes the node and publishes the workflow again.

workflow.description: The metadata.name of a FactoryWorkflow: the workflow the trigger starts.

type.description: What starts the workflow. webhook: a GitHub delivery to the App (event, conditions). finding: a new finding (severity). label: a label added to an issue or pull request (label). kanban: a card moved on the board (fromList, toList). firewall: a sighting from a firewall, Guardian or the GitHub risk rules (source and its filters). manual: only a person pressing Run.

title.description: The trigger node's title in the builder. Left out, the node is titled with metadata.name.

startAt.description: The ids of the steps in the workflow's graph the trigger leads to: one edge from the trigger to each, in this order.

priority.description: The run's priority, 1 (highest) to 5, when runs wait for capacity.

overlap.description: What happens when a run of the workflow for the same subject is already going. Defaults to skip_if_running.

event.description: webhook: the GitHub event, such as push or pull_request, or one action of it, such as pull_request.opened. firewall: one event of the source, such as package.first_seen (or list several in events).

ref.description: webhook push and release events: default for branch pushes, tags for tag pushes and releases.

debounceSeconds.description: webhook and label: deliveries for the same subject inside this window start one run. 0 to 3600; 30 when left out.

maxRunsPerHour.description: webhook, label and firewall: the most runs the trigger starts in an hour, 1 to 1000; 60 when left out.

label.description: label: the issue or pull request label that starts the workflow.

severity.description: finding: the finding severities that start the workflow. All of them when left out.

fromList.description: kanban: the board list a card leaves.

toList.description: kanban: the board list a card enters.

source.description: firewall: where the sighting comes from: the package firewall, the AI firewall, Pix Sandbox egress, Guardian (siem), or the GitHub risk and posture rules.

events.description: firewall: the source's events that start the workflow, such as package.first_seen and package.blocked. Every event of the source when neither this nor event is set.

newTo.description: firewall: only a first sighting in the organisation (org), or, for packages, in the repository (repo).

decision.description: firewall: the firewall decisions that start the workflow, such as block or hold.

ecosystems.description: firewall, package-firewall source: the package ecosystems, such as npm and pypi.

kinds.description: firewall, ai-firewall source: the capability kinds.

sandboxes.description: firewall, egress source: the Pix Sandboxes, by name.

categories.description: firewall, siem source: the Guardian categories.

providers.description: firewall, siem source: the log providers.

tables.description: firewall, siem source: the Guardian tables.

triggers.description: firewall, siem source: the Guardian alert triggers by name.

ticketRepo.description: firewall: the repository, owner/name, where review tickets for a sighting are opened.

conditions.description: webhook: conditions the delivery must meet, all of them. A condition the delivery carries no data for does not match. Globs: * is any run of characters except /, ** includes /, ? is one character; @default is the repository's default branch.

actions.description: The event's actions that count, such as opened and synchronize for pull_request. Only when event names no action.

baseBranch.description: Branch globs the pull request targets, or the pushed branch for a push.

headBranch.description: Branch globs of the pull request's head, or the pushed branch for a push.

paths.description: push only: path globs, at least one of which a pushed commit changed.

pathsIgnore.description: push only: path globs that do not count as a change.

labels.description: Labels on the issue or pull request.

any.description: At least one of these labels.

authorType.description: Who made the change: a person (user), a bot, or any.

draft.description: Draft pull requests: include them, exclude them, or only them.

origin.description: Pull requests from the same repository, from forks, or any.

conclusion.description: check_run, check_suite and workflow_run: the conclusions that count, such as failure. deployment_status: the states that count.

reviewState.description: pull_request_review: the review states that count.

subject.description: What the delivery must be about: a pull request (pr), an issue, nothing in particular (none), or any.

severity.description: dependabot_alert, code_scanning_alert and posture_finding: the alert severities that count.

packageType.description: registry_package: the package types that count, such as container and npm.

properties.description: Repository custom properties: each property named with the values it may hold, such as team: [payments].
